key_insight: A grid-size-invariant surrogate model accurately predicts rock–fluid interaction (interface fluxes and reactions) across resolutions, delivering high-fidelity results at a fraction of the computational cost.
problem_solved: Removes the need for extremely fine numerical grids to capture rock–fluid PDE behaviour, enabling fast multi-query tasks (uncertainty quantification, optimisation) that are infeasible with conventional high-fidelity solvers.
method: Train a surrogate that maps rock/fluid states to interface fluxes/reaction outcomes while explicitly enforcing invariance across grid resolutions.
Use multi-resolution training and scale-aware consistency losses (or an upscaling/downscaling operator) so outputs remain accurate when inputs are coarsened or refined.
Validate surrogate predictions against a high-fidelity PDE solver and measure trade-offs between accuracy and runtime to demonstrate speedups.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to replace expensive PDE solves with a reliable, resolution-robust surrogate for large-scale sensitivity analyses, optimisation, and real-time decision-making in subsurface applications.
visual_elements: Schematic domain showing rock–fluid interface with arrows for fluxes and a caption 'PDE boundary interactions'.

paper_title: Surrogate models for Rock-Fluid Interaction: A Grid-Size-Invariant Approach
paper_authors: Nathalie C. Pinheiro, Donghu Guo, Hannah P. Menke, Aniket C. Joshi, Claire E. Heaney
